issue_1_single_fact_http400.symptom: POST /api/brain-chat {brain:tiny-demo, rich:false} -> HTTP 400 'failed to load brain ... ValueError: non-scalar numpy.ndarray cannot be used for fill'
issue_1_single_fact_http400.root_cause: BACKEND CACHE/ENV MISMATCH in the long-running server. sim.backend.get_backend() is a sticky process-global that ALSO re-reads SIM_BACKEND on every bare call (env always wins). The live server env has SIM_BACKEND=numpy, but sim.bridge bound its module-level cp=cupy at import (sim.bridge._backend_name='cupy'), so EVERY bridge state array is cupy. Two failure points: (a) BridgeParser._train / AttributedBridgeParser._train build cur via get_backend() -> numpy zeros, then assign cp_external_input_current[:] = cur (cupy<-numpy) which cupy routes through .fill() -> 'non-scalar numpy.ndarray cannot be used for fill'; (b) sim.backend.to_host() checks get_backend()=='cupy'; under the numpy env it becomes a no-op passthrough and hands a cupy array to np.asarray -> 'Implicit conversion to a NumPy array is not allowed' (rf_phasor_composer._resonate -> bridge.rf_read_phases).
issue_1_single_fact_http400.proof: Reproduced the exact live traceback via a temp server-side traceback capture (brain_conversational_agent.py:118 cp_external_input_current[:] = cur). Reproduced standalone by flipping the get_backend cache to numpy after importing the cupy bridge -> identical errors; confirmed live DBG: sim.bridge._backend_name='cupy' B.cp=cupy get_backend()='numpy' SIM_BACKEND='numpy'.
fix: webapp/server.py: added _pin_bridge_backend() -- aligns os.environ['SIM_BACKEND'] AND the get_backend() cache to sim.bridge._backend_name (the bridge's REAL backend, cupy on this GPU server) so every get_backend()/to_host() in the chat path is consistent with the cupy bridge arrays. Called at the start of brain_chat and _build_chat_brain. Fixes both (a) and (b) at the source instead of patching each call site.

research/runners/brain_conversational_agent.py: BridgeParser now derives xp from the bridge's OWN array module (cupy.get_array_module(self.bridge.cp_external_input_current)) via a new _bridge_xp() helper, used in __init__/_train/role_of -- so cur ALWAYS matches the bridge regardless of the global cache (belt-and-suspenders).
research/runners/attributed_parser.py: identical _bridge_xp() fix for AttributedBridgeParser (the (noun,'is',adj) attribute-fact parser the self-knowledge brain exercises).

standalone_proof_attributed_path_self_kn.note: Mimics the SK path (BrainConversationalAgent + AttributedBridgeParser 'apple is red' + rf composer + to_host) under the reproduced numpy-env/cupy-bridge mismatch + the pin.

issue_2_rich_too_slow.symptom: POST /api/brain-chat {rich:true} took >75s (http 000 timeout). _get_rich_composer built RichAnswerComposer(neural_planner=on_gpu=True), so the NEURAL dlPFC discourse-planner built + stepped a per-topic SimulationBridge ON THE GPU every turn.
issue_2_rich_too_slow.root_cause: neural_planner=True instantiates NeuralDiscoursePlanner which builds a per-topic spiking bridge per turn -- on the GPU webapp this pushes a turn past the ~75s timeout. The owner prioritizes interactive-console latency.
issue_2_rich_too_slow.fix: webapp/server.py _get_rich_composer now uses neural_planner=False (the HOST gather/order/relevance/breadth/stop planner). With neural_planner=False, NeuralDiscoursePlanner is never instantiated (self._planner=None) so NO per-turn bridge build; the host planner is still SUBSTANTIVE multi-sentence (chain + elaboration, the 'too thin' fix). The direct gate (no-confab MOAT), the role-chase chain hop, and the per-sentence VERIFY are identical either way, so the moat is NOT weakened. The neural planner STAYS the brain_chat_tui --rich default (the 3G flip); ONLY the interactive webapp trades it for latency (commented in code).
